accountSecurity.checkHint: Reads from the ledger who controls the account: its key, or an owner badge. If it is a badge, it also says where that badge lives. Read-only: nothing is signed and nothing is sent.

states.malformed: The bech32m checksum does not add up. Check for a typo before trusting any answer about this address.
states.notAccount: This is a valid address, but not an account. The check only applies to accounts.
states.wrongNetwork: That address belongs to another network. Switch the console to {network} or paste an address from it.

accountSecurity.error: The ledger state could not be read. The account may not exist yet on this network, or the Gateway is unavailable.

key.label: Controlled by its key
key.meaning: Whoever holds the seed phrase holds the account. There is no second factor and no recovery: if the phrase is lost, the account goes with it. This is the state every wallet account starts in.

accessController.label: Shielded by an Access Controller
accessController.meaning: An owner badge governs the account and that badge is held inside an Access Controller, so control follows its roles and a lost factor can be replaced through recovery.

badgeInAccount.label: Securified, badge loose in an account
badgeInAccount.meaning: An owner badge governs the account, and it is sitting in an ordinary account instead of a controller. The account is one transferable NFT: whoever moves it takes the account, and there is no recovery path.

badgeElsewhere.label: Securified, badge held elsewhere
badgeElsewhere.meaning: An owner badge governs the account and it lives outside any Access Controller, in an entity that is not an account. Whatever holds it holds the account.

badgeUnknown.label: Securified, badge not located
badgeUnknown.meaning: The owner rule names the account owner badge, but the Gateway did not report where that badge currently is.

open.label: Open to anyone
open.meaning: The owner role is AllowAll: any transaction can act as the owner of this account.

other.label: Governed by another rule
other.meaning: The owner rule is neither a signature badge nor the account owner badge. Read the rule itself before drawing conclusions.

unknown.label: Could not be determined
unknown.meaning: The owner role could not be read from this account's ledger state.

accountSecurity.controlHint: The account's owner role, as the ledger holds it.

other.custom: A custom rule, with badges this check does not model
other.denyAll: DenyAll: nobody can act as owner

notes.addressRuleMismatch: The public key hash in the owner rule is not the one this address encodes. A preallocated address is the hash of its key, so the two cannot disagree by accident.
notes.badgeHeldBySelf: The owner badge is held by the very account it governs.
notes.singleTransferableBadge: One transferable NFT is the account: no second factor, no recovery, and a transfer is final.
notes.olympiaDerived: Olympia-derived address: it is recovered with the Olympia seed phrase, not the Babylon one.
notes.holderUnresolved: The badge was found in a vault whose owning entity the Gateway did not report.

accountSecurity.controllerHint: The roles that can act on the account, and whether anything is in flight right now.

controller.recoveryInProgress: A recovery proposal is in flight on this controller right now.
controller.withdrawAttempt: Someone is attempting to withdraw the owner badge out of this controller.

multi.title: Multi-factor signing: {need} of {total}
multi.detail: Moving this account takes {need} of its {total} factors together. If one alone is stolen or lost, nobody can use the account with it.

single.title: One factor is enough to sign ({need} of {total})
single.detail: Any of its {total} factors can move the account on its own. If a stolen phone should not be enough, edit the shield in the wallet so signing needs two factors, for example the phone and an Arculus card.

anyone.title: Anyone can sign
anyone.detail: The controller's primary role is AllowAll: anyone can act as the owner of this account. Move the funds to a safe account right away.

nobody.title: Nobody can sign right now
nobody.detail: The primary role is locked (DenyAll). The account can only be used through recovery.

unknown.title: Could not read how many factors it needs
unknown.detail: The primary role's rule has a shape the console cannot interpret. Check it in the wallet.

factorsVerdict.recoveryMulti: Recovering the account takes {need} of {total} factors.
factorsVerdict.recoverySingle: Any one of its {total} factors is enough to recover the account.
factorsVerdict.recoveryOne: A single factor is enough to recover the account.

singleOne.title: A single factor signs for this account
singleOne.detail: The shield guards the account with one factor for signing. If a stolen phone should not be enough, edit it in the wallet so signing needs two factors, for example the phone and an Arculus card.

accountSecurity.levelHint: Where the account sits on a four-level scale, based on who controls it on ledger.

none.label: None
none.meaning: The owner role is AllowAll: anyone can withdraw the funds and change the account.

low.label: Low
low.meaning: A loose owner badge, outside any Access Controller: it is transferable and has no recovery.

basic.label: Basic
basic.meaning: A single key, the seed phrase. It holds as long as the phrase is safe, but there is no second factor and no recovery.

high.label: High
high.meaning: The owner badge lives in an Access Controller: several factors, separate roles and recovery if you lose one.

unknown.label: Undetermined
unknown.meaning: What the ledger returned is not enough to place the account on the scale.

accountSecurity.improveHint: The steps to move up a level, most urgent first. This tool sends nothing: you sign every change from your wallet.
accountSecurity.improveHintShielded: The account is already at the top level. These settings strengthen it further, based on its Access Controller's configuration.
accountSecurity.improveBasics: At any level: never type your seed phrase into a website or share it, read the manifest before signing, and reject transactions you did not start.

abandonOpenAccount.title: Do not use this account
abandonOpenAccount.detail: With AllowAll anyone can withdraw its funds and change its configuration. Send nothing to this address and, if anything of yours depends on it, move it to an account you control.

backupSeedPhrase.title: Keep the seed phrase offline
backupSeedPhrase.detail: Right now the seed phrase is the account. Write it on paper or metal and store it somewhere safe, never in screenshots, phone notes or the cloud. Confirm in the Radix Wallet that the backup is done.

applyShield.title: Apply a security shield
applyShield.detail: In the Radix Wallet, build a security shield from several factors (this device, an Arculus card, a Ledger, a password) and apply it to the account. The owner badge moves into an Access Controller and the account reaches the high level: lose one factor and you recover with the others. Applying it is a transaction with a small XRD fee.

guardBadgeHolder.title: Protect whatever holds the badge
guardBadgeHolder.detail: While the owner badge is loose, this account is only as safe as the entity holding it. Secure that entity and do not sign anything that moves the badge.

moveBadgeToController.title: Put the badge in an Access Controller
moveBadgeToController.detail: Create an Access Controller holding the owner badge, with primary, recovery and confirmation roles built from different factors. It then stops being an NFT that hands the account to whoever receives it.

reviewRule.title: Read the owner rule
reviewRule.detail: This rule is not one this check knows how to judge. Inspect it in the explorer before sending funds: which badges it requires and who holds them.

retryCheck.title: Check it again
retryCheck.detail: It may be a passing Gateway failure, or an account that does not exist on this network yet. Repeat the check in a while and confirm the console is on the address's network.

answerRecovery.title: Review what is in flight
answerRecovery.detail: If you did not start the recovery proposal or the badge withdrawal attempt, act now: cancel or lock it from your wallet with the factors you still hold, before the delay runs out.

addPrimaryFactors.title: Require more than one factor to sign
addPrimaryFactors.detail: A single factor is enough to act as the owner today. Requiring at least two in the primary role means a stolen device is no longer enough to empty the account.

enableTimedRecovery.title: Turn on timed recovery
enableTimedRecovery.detail: With a delay set, the recovery role can complete a recovery without the confirmation role once that time has passed, and the primary role can cancel it meanwhile. It is currently disabled.

fundFeeVault.title: Deposit XRD in the controller
fundFeeVault.detail: The controller has no fee vault. With XRD in it, it can pay for its own recovery even when the account has no funds or you cannot use it.

keepFactorsApart.title: Keep your factors apart
keepFactorsApart.detail: A shield is worth the distance between its factors: do not keep the card, the Ledger and the password in the same place, and check now and then that they still work.

multiSigner.title: What about a multi-signature account?
multiSigner.hint: What can be done today with the Radix Wallet, and why this console does not create multi-signature accounts.

points.title: The wallet only signs with its own keys
points.detail: For two people to approve the same transaction, someone has to gather their signatures and submit it. That needs a separate service coordinating the signers; it is not something a web page can set up without holding anything in custody.

points.title: Setting it up by hand can lock you out
points.detail: Radix Wallet shields use the same mechanism (an Access Controller holding the owner badge). If a website configures one on its own, the wallet may no longer know how to sign for that account, and there is no way back.

points.title: What does work: a shield with several factors
points.detail: Create a shield in the wallet that requires two factors to sign, for example this phone and an Arculus card. If another person keeps the card, no transaction goes out without both. You have to be together to sign, but control is truly shared.

points.title: For group treasuries
points.detail: A DAO or team that votes every payment needs its own component (a multi-signature blueprint) or a governance tool. Review its code or audit before putting funds in.
